title: Backend entry systemdesign url shortener
question: Design a basic URL shortener: a user submits a long URL and gets back a short one, and visiting the short URL redirects to the original.
idealAnswer:
Defines the core data model: a table mapping a short code to the original long URL, plus metadata like creation time

Proposes a way to generate the short code, e.g. a counter converted to base62, or a hash of the URL truncated and checked for collisions, and can explain why the code needs to be short but still have enough space to avoid collisions

Covers both endpoints: POST to create a mapping (returns the short URL), and GET /:code that looks up the mapping and issues an HTTP redirect (3xx) to the original URL

Mentions redirect type tradeoffs, a 301 (permanent) lets browsers cache it and skip hitting the server next time, a 302 (temporary) always hits the server, which matters if you want to track click counts

Bonus: mentions that reads (redirects) vastly outnumber writes (new short URLs) in this system, and that this read-heavy pattern is a natural fit for caching the code-to-URL lookup
